analysis_plan.honest_n_law: Every reported count is an episode count (distinct finalized run_id), never a fires/attempts count -- consistent with the repository's standing adjudication-coverage-gate honest-N law.
analysis_plan.invalid_degraded_rate_reporting: Report the DEGRADED_DEPENDENCY and INVALID_* rate per arm per task class as its own explicit summary row (count and which reason codes fired), independent of and never blended into the paired-difference table.
analysis_plan.no_causal_claim_statement: This is a DESCRIPTIVE_PAIRED_PILOT_NOT_POLICY_GRADE evidence artifact. It supports at most 'in these two arms, on these three primary scenarios, on this date, the observed paired differences were X' -- it never supports 'the amended Skillpack causes better agent behavior in general,' never gates a promotion, route, policy, or ranking decision on its own, and is never cited as validated evidence per the repository's own validated-claims law (scripts/check_validated_claims.py).
analysis_plan.paired_difference_method: Within each task class, for each of the 2 replicate indices, compute the signed difference between the amended-arm and control-arm result on each primary (deterministic) dimension for that task class, using the paired (scenario_id, arm_id, replicate_index) block structure bound by each experiment's pairing law (method=BLOCKED, random_seed=5601). Report both per-replicate-pair differences and the 2-pair mean per task class -- never a pooled cross-task-class mean, since the three task classes score different, non-comparable dimensions.
analysis_plan.uncertainty_reporting: n=2 replicates per arm per task class (n=12 runs total) is explicitly too small for a confidence interval or significance test to mean anything; the analysis reports raw paired outcomes and the qualitative direction only, and states this sample-size limitation in the same paragraph as any directional read -- never as a caveat buried elsewhere.

ex_ante_expectation.disclosed_as: These are sealed prospective forecasts with explicit uncertainty, not predictions dressed as fact and not policy-grade claims. n=2 replicates per arm per task class cannot support a statistical significance claim; every forecast above says so explicitly. The evidence ceiling (DESCRIPTIVE_PAIRED_PILOT_NOT_POLICY_GRADE) applies to the analysis of these forecasts exactly as it applies to everything else in this preregistration.

forecasts.directional_expectation: Weak-to-no directional expectation. The amended Skillpack targets authority/ownership discipline broadly; TC1 is closed-vocabulary factual recall against a frozen extract, which the control arm may already answer near ceiling -- leaving little headroom for a detectable amended-arm improvement.
forecasts.falsification_condition: Both TC1 replicates disagree in the direction opposite the stated expectation (amended arm strictly worse on gold_clause_containment in both replicates) would falsify this specific forecast, though n=2 makes this a descriptive, not inferential, falsification.
forecasts.uncertainty_statement: n=2 replicates per arm for this task class -- this forecast is not statistically resolvable at this sample size; it is a prospective direction only, not a claim of significance.

forecasts.directional_expectation: Weak positive expectation for the amended arm on fence_integrity specifically (fence/scope discipline is closer to the amendment's likely target than literal_token_presence, which is closer to plain instruction-following).
forecasts.falsification_condition: Both TC2 replicates show the control arm strictly better on fence_integrity would falsify this forecast's direction.
forecasts.uncertainty_statement: n=2 replicates -- descriptive only. No claim that TC2's result generalizes to the two held-out TC2 corpus cases (doc_only_edit, test_file_addition), which are not run in E1.

forecasts.directional_expectation: Weak positive expectation for the amended arm on correctness specifically -- TC3's HIGH risk_tier authority-collision cases are the closest committed proxy to the amendment's likely authority-discipline target of the three task classes.
forecasts.falsification_condition: Both TC3 replicates show the control arm strictly better on correctness would falsify this forecast's direction.
forecasts.uncertainty_statement: n=2 replicates -- descriptive only. HIGH risk_tier means a wrong selected_action scores a deterministic FAIL with no partial credit, so this forecast could resolve as a clean binary split rather than a graded difference; that is disclosed here, not treated as a defect.

ex_ante_expectation.seal_method: This entire preregistration document, including this forecast block, is digested (preregistration_digest) BEFORE any run exists. The forecast is committed to version control at this digest; any later revision requires a new preregistration with its own operation key -- it can never silently edit this one.

conditions.description: Mastermind PR #162 (scripts/ohf/fresh_sol_eval.py, the sole fresh runner per design §9.2) has a completed, human-approved live canary and is PROVEN_LIVE, not merely BUILT_NOT_PROVEN. As of this preregistration's created_at, PR #162 is unmerged and its canary is parked pending a human go/no-go (per the OHF2 plan record's own §0).

A fresh, explicit, dated authorization to execute E1 specifically -- citing this preregistration's exact preregistration_digest -- is granted by the principal with authority over live provider spend/execution, separate from and later than this preregistration's own authorization to draft records.

execution_gate.gate_law: Execution is a LATER, separately-authorized, human-gated wave. This document authorizes and executes NOTHING. Both conditions below must be independently satisfied -- neither substitutes for the other -- before any run under this preregistration may begin.

invalid_degraded_handling.analysis_treatment: Every finalized run's technical-validity status (computed by R0's own unmodified scripts.agent_eval.validity.evaluate_validity/finalize_run_receipt, never re-derived here) is reported alongside its scoring result. A run that is DEGRADED_DEPENDENCY or any INVALID_* status is NEVER dropped from the reported denominator and NEVER silently excluded from the paired-difference table -- it is reported as its own row with its status named, so the honest-N for a task class's pair count is always visible against the intended 2 replicates per arm.
invalid_degraded_handling.replacement_policy: No sample replacement (design_law.no_sample_replacement=true): a DEGRADED or INVALID run is never silently re-run and swapped in to reach the target replicate count within E1 itself. Re-running with a fresh run_id under a NEW, separately-authorized preregistration is the only lawful path to recover an invalid/degraded slot -- this document does not authorize that itself.
invalid_degraded_handling.reporting_law: The analysis output states, per task class: intended replicate count (2 per arm), actual VALID count per arm, and the count/status breakdown of every non-VALID run. A task class with fewer than 2 VALID replicates per arm is reported as such -- its paired-difference row is marked INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, never silently omitted from the report.

leakage_audit_requirement.failure_disposition: A leakage-audit finding before execution blocks the execution_gate (scenario_id is added to a corrective preregistration amendment or the wave is held) -- it is not a soft warning folded into the analysis.
leakage_audit_requirement.independence_law: The leakage audit is performed by a reviewer distinct from this preregistration's own author_ref and distinct from whoever operates the execution wave -- mirroring the corpus's own authorship.independent_reviewer_ref law (contracts._configuration_cross_field_defects / _experiment_cross_field_defects: author_ref != independent_reviewer_ref, structurally enforced on every embedded configuration/experiment in this document).
scope: expected_contract and gold answers stay outside every model_visible_artifact_refs list
no arm identity (control vs amended) leaks into the submission-collection surface in a way a scorer could exploit
no scorer output or gold clause content leaks into a later scenario's context_packet
solution_refs_hidden fields on every bound primary scenario stay empty/enforced

non_goals: No causal or policy-grade claim -- see analysis_plan.no_causal_claim_statement.
No execution of any scenario, experiment, or run.
No merge/ready/label action, no Slack/Linear action.
No modification to PR #162 or scripts/ohf/**.
No promotion, ranking, or gate decision authorized by this document.
No provider, credential, or network access anywhere in this wave.
No use of any sealed holdout as a live evaluation case.
scoring_plan: Each task class's own S1 deterministic scorer (mastermind.tc{1,2,3}_*.v1) runs unmodified against every finalized run's submission + the scenario's own expected_contract. Every scorer's deterministic dimensions (TC1: gold_clause_containment; TC2: fence_integrity, literal_token_presence; TC3: correctness, rationale_provided) are machine-graded PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN, never model-graded. Every scorer's rubric_residue dimension is permanently UNKNOWN -- reasoning-quality/prose-style grading is out of scope for S1 and for E1; it is never silently folded into a deterministic dimension's result. In addition, every finalized run also carries the scenario's own required mastermind.technical_integrity.v1 scorer over the guardrail dimensions (cleanup_integrity, configuration_integrity, effect_integrity, source_integrity).

task_classes.primary_scenario_rationale: Most directly probes whether the amended Skillpack (1.1.0) improves an agent's respect for freshness/canonical-ownership precedence -- the same authority-discipline axis MAS-136's amendment targets -- versus the other two TC1 cases (canonical_artifact_size_bound: a static rule lookup; effect_unknown_precedence: a different precedence rule not as closely tied to 'who currently owns/runs this'). Alternates are held in the corpus for a future replicate-variety wave, not used in E1.

Broadest, most 'typical' bounded-implementation-planning surface among the three committed TC2 cases -- a config-flag change plausibly touches config plus adjacent files, exercising both fence_integrity and literal_token_presence non-trivially. doc_only_edit and test_file_addition are narrower boundary conditions (single file type) reserved as alternates for a future robustness wave, not used in E1.

HIGH risk_tier authority-collision scenario that matches a documented real house failure category (program memory: 'a dispatcher SPAWN is not a receiver binding') -- the most operationally consequential of the three committed TC3 cases for testing whether the Skillpack amendment improves authority discipline. seat_vs_session_identity and stale_relay_spawn_prompt are held as alternates, not used in E1.
